answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a mirror as the anchor of the cost.
